知り合いに、外国語を流暢に使いこなす人が一人います。その人はよくほかの人から「外国でどれくらい暮らしたんですか」と言われるそうです。ところがその人は一度も外国で暮らしたことはなく、長くても1週間ほど旅行した経験があるくらいだそうです。

It's very important to think critically when forming and revising beliefs. It doesn't make sense to take whatever a scientist says is true on faith.

However in this case, I don't believe any convincing argument can be made that this is a fossilized footprint. I look at it like this:

What is more likely?

  • This is the first known example of granite forming gradually from a softer material, on the surface of the earth, and at some point in this miraculous process a giant (a creature for which no other evidence exists) stepped on it?
  • This granite formed like all other granite (by magma cooling into stone under the earth and later erupting) and the foot-like shape got there by some means other than a foot?

In my view, the latter option is far more likely. It doesn't require us to come up with new explanations for a large set of findings central to geology, and it doesn't require us to explain why there is no other evidence of giants ever having existed - it only requires us to explain how a foot-like shape got carved into granite.

That's easy enough - somebody could have carved it, or some natural process could have formed it. Even if those things are extremely unlikely to have occurred, they are far more likely than giants evolving but leaving only one footprint as evidence while geologists were wrong about how rock forms for the last century.

where do I turn when my questions and those of the alternative researchers around the world are laughed out of scientific circles?

In some cases, you could acknowledge that it was a bad idea and move on.

But if it is indeed a case of a good idea being rejected for bad reasons (e.g. it doesn't fit the dominant worldview of scientists in a particular time and place), then there is a problem. The scientific community does have serious flaws, and there are many great hypotheses that it can't test (or that can't even be conceived properly) because of ideological constraints.

So what do you do? I don't know; it depends on the question. Science remains the best way of modeling reality available, but it is very hard to do without willing colleagues. Some questions may have to remain unasked until certain ideological constraints can be loosened up.

That said, I don't believe this footprint is an example of such a question - it is a question that doesn't even need posing, because the answer is already quite clear. It's a fake.
